reasoning_traces.think:
Apodictic certainty arises when complete information allows deterministic outcome prediction—akin to mathematical axioms. Estimative judgment emerges where uncertainty prevails, requiring probabilistic estimation. Intuitive reasoning reflects bounded rationality, where decisions are made via heuristics rather than exhaustive analysis. These three forms define a triadic structure: certainty (axiomatic), estimation (probabilistic), and intuition (heuristic). Their interplay reveals dualities in decision-making frameworks—logical consistency versus pragmatic adaptability. Failure modes include overconfidence in apodictic models, misalignment in estimative frameworks, and bias in intuitive judgments. The epistemological tension lies in reconciling these modes within unified inference engines.
